content:
iOS 27 is a major update to the Apple Photos app, bringing improvements to slideshow playback, Shared Albums, and more. It also adds a long-awaited camera roll–style feature called “Captured by Me.”

In iOS 27, the Photos app’s “Captured by Me” only includes photos and videos you take with the Camera app.

Apple’s Photos app has been expanding its functionality for years. Beyond storing the photos and videos you take on your iPhone, it also includes content shared with you by others, “Memories,” screenshots, saved media, and much more.

In the past, the Photos app offered a “Camera Roll” album similar to today’s “Recents” album, containing both photos you took and photos you saved.

But for a long time, a feature that truly shows only the photos and videos you personally took—in other words, a more accurately named “Camera Roll”—has been missing.

iOS 27 finally brings that long-missing feature, called “Captured by Me.”

In iOS 27, “Captured by Me” is a brand-new collection that, as the name suggests, contains only media you took with the Camera app.

That means the photos and videos you capture with your iPhone are gathered in one place, but you won’t see screenshots, images friends sent you, or other types of content.

In addition to this dedicated “Captured by Me” collection, you can also use the “Captured by Me” filter in the main Photos library.

No matter how you use it, “Captured by Me” in iOS 27 fills an important gap in Apple’s Photos features.

Are you planning to use this new Apple Photos feature in iOS 27? Let us know in the comments.
